findings.evidence: Lines 155-164 define the instance by `smul σ x := galoisScalarMap H σ x`; grep for `smul` in the file yields only `galoisScalarMap_smul` (k̄-semilinearity), `val_smul` (GroupLike level, line 186) and `smul_ofMul` (line 207) — no ring-level `smul` restatement.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem smul_def (σ) (x) : σ • x = galoisScalarMap H σ x := (rfl)` and `@[simp] theorem smul_tmul (σ) (a) (h) : σ • (a ⊗ₜ[k] h) = σ.toAlgHom a ⊗ₜ[k] h`, plus the `toMul_smul : (σ • x).toMul = σ • x.toMul` companion to `smul_ofMul`.
findings.issue: `instGaloisScalarMulSemiringAction` makes `σ • x` the user-facing notation on `AlgebraicClosure k ⊗[k] H`, but no lemma bridges it to `galoisScalarMap`: `galoisScalarMap_tmul` (line 62) has head `galoisScalarMap`, so neither `simp` nor `rw` touches `σ • (a ⊗ₜ[k] h)`. The instance has no consumer and no API in the repo. The same gap on the additive lattice: `smul_ofMul` (line 207) only fires when the term is syntactically `Additive.ofMul _`, so `(σ • x).toMul` is unreachable.

findings.evidence: `geometricCharacterGroupEquiv_symm_apply_val` (line 62) gives `x.val = 1 ⊗ₜ[k] MonoidAlgebra.single g 1`, and `galoisScalarMap_tmul` sends it to `σ.toAlgHom 1 ⊗ₜ single g 1 = 1 ⊗ₜ single g 1`; grep for `smul|•` across the four CharacterLattice files returns no hit outside `CommHopfAlgCat/CharacterLattice.lean`.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem smul_eq_self (σ : Field.absoluteGaloisGroup k) (x : CommHopfAlgCat.geometricCharacterGroup (coordinateRing k G).obj) : σ • x = x`, provable from `val_smul`, `geometricCharacterGroupEquiv_symm_apply_val` and `galoisScalarMap_tmul` with `map_one`; restate it for `splitTorusCharacterLatticeEquiv` on the additive lattice.
findings.issue: None of the three character identifications (`geometricCharacterGroupEquiv`, `splitTorusCharacterLatticeEquiv`, `exists_characterLattice_addEquiv_of_torus`) is related to the Galois action the PR introduces, so the action is never computed on a single object. In particular the defining fact for the split case — the action on the character group of a diagonalizable coordinate ring is trivial — is absent, leaving `•` inert for every consumer.

findings.evidence: The missing lemma forces the detour at `TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/DiagonalizableGroup/CharacterLattice.lean:66-76`, which recovers the inverse value via `apply_symm_apply` plus a three-step `calc` instead of a direct rewrite.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem val_groupLikeEquiv_symm (h : H) : ((groupLikeEquiv (R := R) (H := H)).symm h).val = _root_.MonoidAlgebra.single h 1 := (rfl)` in this file.
findings.issue: `groupLikeEquiv` exposes only the forward characterization (`groupLikeEquiv_apply_eq_iff`, `eq_single_groupLikeEquiv`); the value of the inverse, `(groupLikeEquiv.symm h).val = MonoidAlgebra.single h 1`, is missing, and the body is not exposed, so downstream cannot get it by `rfl`.

findings.evidence: Lines 179-185 and 189-194: both carry `@[simp]`; the second's LHS `x.val` is unconditional in `x`. `TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/DiagonalizableGroup/CharacterLattice.lean:56` uses `simp only [...]` with an explicit lemma list rather than `simp`.
findings.fix: Drop `@[simp]` from `eq_single_groupLikeEquiv` (keep it as a plain lemma) and let `groupLikeEquiv_apply_eq_iff` be the simp-normal characterization.
findings.issue: `eq_single_groupLikeEquiv` is `@[simp]` with LHS the bare projection `x.val`, so it rewrites every group-like value in a monoid algebra and immediately de-normalizes the output of the other new `@[simp]` lemma `groupLikeEquiv_apply_eq_iff`: the goal `groupLikeEquiv x = h` becomes `x.val = single h 1` and then `single (groupLikeEquiv x) 1 = single h 1`. It also competes with `GroupLike.val_mapEquiv` on `(mapEquiv e x).val`.

findings.evidence: Line 28 vs the signature at line 56 (`→ₐ[k]`) and the separate semilinear map at line 94.
findings.fix: Describe `galoisScalarMap` as the `k`-algebra map on the scalar factor, and list `galoisScalarSemilinearMap`, `instGaloisScalarMulSemiringAction` and `instGeometricCharacterGroupGaloisAction`/`instCharacterLatticeGaloisAction` in Main declarations.
findings.issue: The module header describes `galoisScalarMap` as "the semilinear absolute-Galois action", but it is a `k`-algebra hom; the semilinear packaging is the separate `galoisScalarSemilinearMap`, and the two action instances — the actual user-facing surface — are not listed at all.

summary: The Galois action is exposed as three parallel surfaces (`galoisScalarMap`, `galoisScalarSemilinearMap`, two `•` instances) but nothing computes `•` at the ring level or relates it to any of the character identifications, so no consumer can evaluate the action even on a split torus. `groupLikeEquiv` also lacks its inverse-value lemma, and one of its new `@[simp]` lemmas de-normalizes the other.
